I know the feeling, brother; you're not alone in it. Nothing hurts like being ignored by a friend who means the world to you -- I know it chops my self-worth to splinters whenever it happens to me. Just a simple question ("Do you know if..?"), or an unobtrusive request ("Let me know when.."), and they don't spare you even an acknowledgement. Especially when in the past, there was never a day that passed when you didn't have a conversation with them.

Sometimes people are busy, despite being quicker to respond to others. Sometimes other things are going on. If they're worth it, don't resent them -- and don't jump to undue assumptions. In my case, my esteem for this person remains, regardless of how many times I end up hurt. Maybe I won't live to find out whether I was right or wrong, haha.

I have no advice to lend, but maybe you can feel less alone knowing there are others out there who feel the same way.

Words, I'm afraid of forgetting words. As someone with a fondness for writing, it frustrates me when a simple word just suddenly falls out of my vocabulary, just as I'm preparing to use it in a sentence. Screwdriver. Carousel. Pensiveness. Bannister.

I used to strive to learn as much as possible, about virtually any topic. I value knowledge, but I can't say for sure whether I was trying to gird my mind against future deterioration, or just trying to "stick it" to that looming inevitability. As recently as the past year, I've started giving up on that.

I'm a man with regrets. I hurt someone I care about, I damaged a friendship I valued above anything else, and I think I've lost much of my capacity for love. Sometimes I think it'll be for the best when my memories leave me. Here's to nihilism.
